1
This is an application for regular bail filed by the sole accused in crime No.303/2024 of Kadinamkulam Police Station, Thiruvananthapuram under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
I have perused the report of the Investigating Officer placed by the learned Public Prosecutor.

3. The prosecution case is that the accused herein subjected the defacto complainant for forceful sexual intercourse on three days, viz., on a day during March, 2020, on a day during April, 2021 and third one on 28.11.2023, after putting cloth on her mouth and thereby committed offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 376AB, 451 of the Indian Penal Code, Sections 4(2) r/w 3(a),
6(1) r/w 5(l), 5(m), 5(n), 8 r/w 7, 10 r/w 9(l) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (`PoCSO Act' for short).
4.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that 3 occurrences are stated in the F.I statement, viz. on a day during March, 2020, on a day during April, 2021 and third one on 28.11.2023.

It is pointed out, referring the date of birth of the accused as 04.08.2004, that when he committed sexual molestation, as alleged by the prosecution during March, 2020 and April, 2021,
the accused did not complete 18 years.
However, it is submitted that as on the date of the third occurrence on 28.11.2023, the accused attained majority.
Highlighting these points, the learned counsel pressed for grant of regular bail to the petitioner, who has been in custody from 17.04.2024 onwards.

5. Whereas it is submitted by the learned Public Prosecutor that this crime was registered as on 17.04.2024, after commission of offence by the accused on 28.11.2023 and, therefore, mentioning of 2 similar occurrences during juvenility of the petitioner would not absolve him from criminal prosecution otherwise since the occurrence as on 28.11.2023 is the foundation of this case and on that day the accused attained majority.
6.
Going by the birth certificate placed by the learned counsel for the petitioner, his date of birth is 04.08.2004.
If so, the occurrences on a day during March, 2020 and on a day during April, 2021 are instances when he was a minor.
But the last incident is the immediate cause for registering this crime.
Since he attained majority as on the date of the third occurrence on 28.11.2023, he could not get any benefit on the ground of his juvenility with regard to previous occurrences.

7. Coming to the facts of this case, it is discernible from the F.I statement given by the defacto complainant that the accused herein is none other than the son of the elder sister of the mother of the victim.
The victim was subjected to rape and aggravated sexual assault, that too, after putting cloth on the mouth of the victim, in order to prevent her from crying or calling anybody for her rescue.
On 28.11.2023, he forcefully subjected sexual intercourse to the minor victim and the accused attained majority as on 28.11.2023.

8. The facts of the case would reveal that the accused is a close relative, being the son of the elder sister of the victim's mother, and in a case involving very serious allegations of aggravated sexual Xxxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88845921/
2 assault, if the petitioner is released on bail, fair trial could not be secured.
The petitioner, being a relative of the victim, if released on bail, there is likelihood of threatening the witnesses, including the victim.
In such view of the matter, the petitioner is not liable to be released in a case of this nature, since trial keeping him in custody is necessary.
Accordingly, this bail application stands dismissed.

Sd/-
(A. BADHARUDEEN, JUDGE) rtr/
